text:
alice (runtime): hey team, noticed a 8-12% p99 regression on short-seq traffic after yesterday's kernel-autotune roll. snapshots attached in thread.
ben (scheduling): saw that on the dashboard too, looks concentrated on 1-8 token responses.
alice (runtime): exact repro on staging with rxl-7b small prompt mix. baseline (pre-roll) p99 ~42ms; post-roll ~48-50ms.
carmen (perf): can you dump kernel selection logs for a hot request? esp interested in launch estimates vs steady-state.
dmitri (autotune): uploading recent autotune decisions — we bumped preference for large-vector matmul path on aarch64 because it was better for throughput on long seqs. maybe sticky path is hijacking short seqs.
alice (runtime): here's one log snippet from a failing request:
```
[2026-03-16T09:03:12Z] kernel_picker: model=rxl-7b seq=6 batch=3 samples=120
selected=matmul_vec_v3 score=0.82 launch_ms=2.1 steady_ms=0.6 reason=autotune_win
cache_hit=false kv_status=warm
```
ben (scheduling): launch_ms 2.1 is killer for short sequences — steady only 0.6 but launch dominates. continuous batching reduced some of that but not enough.
elaine (infra): is the launch measured from CUDA context init or kernel upload? we switched some DMA paths last week.
carmen (perf): I ran microbench on both kernels on the same host: matmul_vec_v3 launch ~2.0ms, matmul_small_v1 launch ~0.4ms; steady-state matmul_vec_v3 0.55ms vs small_v1 0.8ms. So for short seqs small_v1 wins overall.
dmitri (autotune): current autotuner objective prioritized steady-state throughput mainly (longtest), we didn't weight startup overhead. that's the bug.
alice (runtime): interesting interaction: continuous batching tends to keep KV cache warm and forces selection to large vector kernel because it reduces per-token time for long tails, but for bursts of sub-10 tokens the initial launch penalty is exposed.
ben (scheduling): could we make scheduler include 'expected tokens remaining' in routing so we prefer low-launch kernels for short-horizon requests? or add a per-request override if len(prompt)+expected_out < threshold.
dmitri (autotune): quick patch idea: add a launch_penalty term to kernel score: score' = score - alpha * launch_ms / (avg_seq_len + 1). alpha tunable per workload. will try.
carmen (perf): before we change autotuner, can we force candidate kernel with env override to validate? e.g. REDWOOD_KERNEL_HINT=matmul_small_v1 on staging.
elaine (infra): deploy-bot: can you trigger a canary with env=REDWOOD_KERNEL_HINT=matmul_small_v1 on rxl-7b-staging?
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for rxl-7b-staging with REDWOOD_KERNEL_HINT=matmul_small_v1.
carmen (perf): ran 30m load replay with small hint: p99 down to 43ms (near baseline), throughput -2% for long seq tail but small seqs much better.
ben (scheduling): so tradeoff confirmed. We need a routing+autotune combo: schedule short jobs to small kernel, long jobs to vec kernel, and maybe keep dynamic fallback if queue lengths spike.
dmitri (autotune): I'll prototype adding sequence-length-aware scoring and a per-model alpha. can we get labeled traffic distribution per customer?
alice (runtime): I'll add a route policy flag 'favor_low_launch=true' and wire it to the selector as a soft hint. also add metrics: kernel_choice, launch_ms, steady_ms by seq_bin.
carmen (perf): also add a pprof flame for the 2.1ms launch path — need to confirm it's GPU-init and not something in the runtime thread.
elaine (infra): FYI I rolled back the DMA microchange to the testing image to exclude infra confounding factors.
dmitri (autotune): quick experiment results: alpha=0.7 reduces short p99 by 6% without regressing long-seq throughput more than 1.5%. will push candidate tomorrow.
alice (runtime): plan: (1) short-term canary with kernel hint for affected customers, (2) merge autotune scoring update with alpha fallback, (3) add routing hint and metrics, (4) follow-up perf run and decision.
ben (scheduling): agree. add an alert if p99 improves but long-seq tail drops >5%.
carmen (perf): will own the perf run and dashboard. dropping a checklist in #eng-releases once candidate pushed. :+1:
dmitri (autotune): noted. thanks for quick triage.
alice (runtime): thanks everyone. saving logs to the ticket and will link PR soon. :eyes:
